newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Parcelforce and KLM sign express deal.
newsitem.headline: Parcelforce and KLM sign express deal.

text.p: KLM Cargo has just signed an agreement to handle the express mail services (EMS) of the British Post Office's Parcelforce unit in the Netherlands, a KLM Cargo spokesman told Reuters.
For the past three years the EMS Parcelforce consignments were handled by KPN, the Dutch Post office, a KPN spokesman said.
According to KPN, its recent acquisition of TNT Express Worldwide, was not the reason for Parcelforce's choice.
The spokesman from the Dutch airline said this deal is related to a much larger contract that KLM recently won.

KLM Cargo bid successfully for a tender to handle the EMS shipments of Contract Management Team (CMT), a group of 50 post offices in a general agreement effective January 1. CMT is a member of the Universal Postal Union (UPU).
That deal means the Dutch airline handles 17,500 EMS shipments a month from the post offices, said the spokesman.
"In a couple of years we expect this to double," he said.
KLM Cargo's Parcelforce agreement is just another example of one of the 50 CMT post offices signing an additional individual contract with the Dutch airline, he said.

"Half of these (CMT) post offices have already signed individual agreements with KLM (within the framework of the general agreement) and we expect this to grow to around 40 organisations in the coming months," he said.
Often the individual organisations have special requirements so they sign these separate agreements, said the spokesman.
KLM Cargo has subcontracted the road transportation to Dutch Parcel Service (NPD).

The KLM spokesman added: "We are the only airline to have signed an agreement with CMT and we feel our bid was successful because CMT realised that KLM can offer the total package and handle the EMS product punctually." -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
